Getting started

Connect your software

Move from a detected installation to a fresh connection with the exact host and document you chose.

  • Before you begin
  • Follow the steps
  • Check the result
  • If something goes wrong
  • Continue with a related guide

Before you begin

  • An eligible Vector OS build and a separately licensed, exactly supported Rhino or Revit installation.
  • An eligible connector package for that exact app/host/runtime lane.
  • Save important work and be ready to close affected host instances when configuration requires it.

Follow the steps

  1. Choose how to find the host

    Open bundled Connect. Use its disclosed local detection, choose Manual locate for an executable you installed, or defer setup. Detection does not scan your projects or start the host.

    Checkpoint: You see no host, an unsupported candidate, or uniquely labelled version/path choices.

  2. Select one eligible installation

    Choose the intended host/version explicitly. Read Requirements for an unsupported candidate; selecting a file path alone is not compatibility proof.

    Checkpoint: Connect identifies the exact eligible installation rather than guessing between versions.

  3. Review and install the connector

    Read the package publisher, version, size, permissions and compatibility. Use the built-in verified installation flow.

    Checkpoint: The package receipt confirms installation. If the host is absent, the state remains installed/configure later, not Connected.

  4. Configure and restart normally

    Follow the host-specific configuration plan. Save and close all affected host instances when requested, then perform the normal restart. Do not change unrelated plugins or add-in files yourself.

    Checkpoint: Configuration is read back and any restart requirement is satisfied.

  5. Open the intended document

    Use the explicitly offered host launch action or open your host normally, then open your document in the host. Choose the exact live process and document in Connect.

    Checkpoint: The selected document label, units and current host identity match your intended work.

  6. Test the fresh connection

    Use Connect/test and wait for an authenticated handshake and current capability result.

    Checkpoint: Connected is tied to that live process and document. A running process, installed package or successful restart alone is insufficient.

Check the result

  • Connect reports a fresh authenticated connection for the selected host/document with the capabilities it actually exposes.
  • No native model change is needed to establish the connection.

If something goes wrong

  • No host is detected or more than one version appears.

    Refresh after installation or manually locate the intended executable. Select a unique eligible candidate; do not use an unsupported Configure workaround.

    Resume from: Exact host installation selection.

  • The package is tampered, its metadata expired or installation response is lost.

    Stop. Keep the package identity and original lifecycle reference. Inspect the installation journal/inventory before another attempt.

    Resume from: Known package/registration state.

  • The host starts but the plugin is missing or trust is blocked.

    Inspect the stated runtime/trust/configuration problem. Keep host protections enabled and use repair guidance for that build.

    Resume from: Verified registration followed by a fresh handshake.

  • Connection drops during a write.

    Pause affected document writes and reconcile the original operation. Reconnect refreshes identity; it must not replay the edit.

    Resume from: Original outcome, then fresh document binding.

Availability and verification

Connect is an installed desktop workflow. The website preview and software directory do not connect to a host or establish version support.

Source-backed workflow; installed walkthrough not verified.

  • No host launch, plugin registration or handshake was run.
